title: Proof
body_md:
At each fixed $n$, Proposition~\ref{app:fixed} supplies the quadratic
renormalizations and auxiliary integrability in
\cite[Proposition~3.1]{PW}. We trace the estimates in its Sections~4--6.
Write $(r,v)$ for one selected solution and set
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 M=\int_\Omega r_0,\qquad
 K=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_t\int_\Omega r|v|^2,\qquad
 D=\int_{Q_T}|\nabla v|^2,\\
 P=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_t\int_\Omega p_\delta(r),\qquad
 J=\|r_0v_0\|_1.
 \end{gathered}
\]
These quantities are uniform in $n$ by \eqref{app:initialenergy} and
\eqref{app:uniformenergy}; in particular $J\le\sqrt{MK_0}$.

\emph{Radon and negative half-derivative bounds.}
In \cite[Section~4]{PW}, the smoothed one-dimensional density
primitive is bounded by $C_\zeta M$. Endpoint momentum terms use
$C_\zeta M(J+\sqrt{MK})$; the inertia and pressure cutoff terms use
$C_\zeta TM(K+P)$, and viscous cutoff terms use
$C_\zeta M\sqrt{TD}$. The principal stress is bounded by
$C_\zeta\sqrt D\sqrt Z$, where $Z$ is the smoothed squared Radon norm.
The principal inertia remainder is nonnegative by the linewise
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. Consequently,
\[
 Z\le C_{\zeta,T,\Omega}(M,K,D,P,J)+C_\zeta\sqrt D\sqrt Z.
\]
Young's inequality closes this bound uniformly in the line direction
and smoothing scale. Removing smoothing gives \eqref{app:Radon};
\cite[Lemma~2.1 and Proposition~5.1]{PW} then give
\eqref{app:halfderivative}.

\emph{Finite potential exponents.}
On a containing ball let $I_1$ denote the potential with kernel
$|x|^{-1}$, and put
$Q=I_1(\zeta r)$, $L=I_1(\zeta r|v|^2)$.
The half-derivative estimate gives $Q\in L^2_tL^4_x$ locally;
kinetic energy gives $L\in L^\infty_tL^s_x$ for $1<s<2$.
Each component $F$ of the momentum potentials in
\cite[Section~5.1, Lemmas~5.1--5.2]{PW} satisfies $|F|\le C\sqrt{QL}$, hence
$F\in L^4_tL^q_x$ for $q<8/3$. The Sobolev multiplication estimate
\cite[Lemma~2.2]{PW} also gives
$F\in L^1_tL^{4/(1+2\sigma)}_x$ for $0<\sigma<1/2$.
Interpolation with weights $2/3$ and $1/3$, choosing $q$ close to
$8/3$ and $\sigma$ small, therefore yields
\begin{equation}\label{appendix:PWpotential}
 F\in L^2_tL^q_x\quad\text{for every }2<q<3,
\end{equation}
with norms controlled by the same budget and localization.

\emph{Local pressure-density gain.}
Take $\psi(r)=(1+r)^\alpha-1$ in
\cite[Section~6]{PW}. Then
$|\psi(r)|+|r\psi'(r)-\psi(r)|\le C_\alpha r^\alpha$.
Mass and dissipation bound the renormalization source in
$L^2_tL^{2/(1+2\alpha)}_x$. The localized potential
$\mathcal H=\nabla\Delta^{-1}(\zeta\psi(r))$ satisfies
\[
 \|\mathcal H\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}}
 +\|\nabla\mathcal H\|_{L^\infty_tL^{1/\alpha}_x}\le C_{
 \zeta,\alpha,\Omega}(M),
\]
by finite-exponent potential estimates. Choose
$q=2/(1-2\alpha)<3$. The critical potential terms close using
\eqref{appendix:PWpotential} and
\[
 \frac1q+\frac12+\alpha=1.
\]
At $\alpha=1/8$ these exponents are $8/3$, $2$ and $8$,
while the source exponent is $8/5$. Cutoff pressure, inertia and
stress terms are controlled by $P,K,D$ and the preceding potential
bounds. The time endpoint terms satisfy
\[
 |\Gamma_T|\le C_\zeta\|\mathcal H\|_\infty
 \left(\|r_0v_0\|_1+\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_t\|rv(t)\|_1\right)
 \le C_\zeta\|\mathcal H\|_\infty(J+\sqrt{MK}).
\]
Thus no initial velocity Sobolev norm or density lower bound enters
the final constants.

Spatial mollification is removed at each fixed $n$ before asserting
uniformity. At this stage $rv\in L^2(Q_T)$, and the commutator
$[\zeta\psi(r)v]_h-[\zeta\psi(r)]_hv$ tends to zero in $L^2$;
this follows from strong mollifier convergence and time dominated
convergence, using $\psi(r)\in L^\infty_tL^4_x$ and
$v\in L^2_tL^4_x$. The bounded $L^2$ operator
$\nabla\operatorname{div}\Delta^{-1}$ therefore removes the remainder
in \cite[Section~6, (80), (99)--(100), pp.~26, 31--32]{PW}. This fixed-$n$ use of the
momentum norm introduces no outer-uniform high-power requirement.
Since $r^\alpha\le C_\alpha(1+\psi(r))$, the bound for
$\int\zeta^2p_\delta(r)\psi(r)$ and the pressure budget $TP$ give
\eqref{app:localgain}. Its constants
have precisely the dependence stated in Lemma~\ref{app:PW}.
